title: Remote Inbound Sales Representative
description: Please Read the Whole Job Description Before Applying. At Meadow, we’re reimagining end-of-life care - a $23B industry untouched by modern software or service thinking. In under a year, we became the largest cremation provider in Los Angeles, with 80+ NPS and hundreds of families served monthly. Now we’re scaling across the U.S. and hiring globally. We believe great people live everywhere. Our team works across continents and time zones, grounded by shared values: high standards, deep empathy, and a drive to do work that matters. Learn more about our global teams here: ---------- If this sounds like your kind of team, we'd love to hear from you. About the Role As an Inbound Sales Representative, you’ll be the first voice families hear when they reach out. You’ll guide them with clarity and compassion -  no cold calls or pushy tactics, just meaningful conversations that help people make one of life’s most important decisions with confidence. You’ll manage warm, inbound leads from first contact to close, helping families feel confident in their decisions and supported every step of the way. Every call is a chance to make someone’s life a little easier, and every conversation reflects our standard of unmatched hospitality. A quick note, because many candidates wonder about it: People often assume this work is emotionally heavy, but our team consistently finds it deeply meaningful and surprisingly uplifting. The role is rooted in hospitality, clarity, and human connection, not sadness. Rather than feeling heavy, the work offers a unique sense of purpose as part of a modern, compassionate company transforming an outdated industry and bringing dignity, transparency, and warmth to families across the country. What You’ll Do - Own warm inbound leads end-to-end - from first call to close - using Meadow's consultative playbook. - Guide families through cremation options with clarity and care, helping them make a confident decision in a single conversation when possible. - Run a disciplined follow-up rhythm across phone, text, and email so no family falls through the cracks. - Hit revenue targets while holding strong close rates and quality scores. - Move fluently across our stack - HubSpot, Aircall, GSuite, Slack, and our case management system. Requirements - 2+ years of B2C sales experience - Strong written and spoken English. - Confident, empathetic communicator who explains clearly, listens well, and excels on the phone. - Self-driven seller motivated by both impact and performance; emotionally steady and highly coachable. - Comfortable working independently and managing a consistent follow-up rhythm. - Familiarity with HubSpot or comparable CRMs (Salesforce, Zoho, etc.). - A home setup that supports the work - see our tech requirements for details. Bonus Points - Experience selling in high-trust categories (insurance, healthcare, travel, etc.). - Spanish fluency -  many of the families we serve speak it. Details: - Remote, full-time - Compensation: $6-$9 OTE - Base rate plus a real, sizable bonus tied to deals closed, conversion performance, and overall team success. - Targets are designed to be hit, with additional bonus opportunities beyond OTE for top performers. - Tools: HubSpot (CRM), Aircall (phone), Slack, and our case management system - Schedule: - Full-time, 8-hour shifts on a consistent weekly schedule - Days: Monday–Friday, Tuesday–Saturday, or Sunday–Thursday (weekend availability a plus) - Available shift windows: - AM (start 6–8am EST) - PM (start 1–4pm EST) - Night (start 8–10pm EST) Why You’ll Love Working With Us: - We’re a real business, built to last. We’ve proven our model in LA and became the largest independent funeral home in California in less than two years.  We’re now going national. And plan to grow for years to come. - A serious employer for global teammates. We have years of experience running distributed teams. Same 1:1s, check-ins, and career paths as our U.S. team - same expectations, same opportunities. - People stay. Regrettable turnover is very low. Don't take our word for it - read our Glassdoor reviews. - Fair compensation with real upside. Base pay benchmarked globally. Top performers consistently earn the full bonuses. - High care, high standards. Real investment in training and growth, honest feedback, no burnout culture. - Benefits: PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid training, fully remote. - Purpose-driven work: Real impact during one of life's most meaningful transitions. Apply Now We’re just getting started, and we’re looking for people who want to grow with us. If you’re excited about making an impact, building meaningful relationships, and launching a successful career in sales and tech, apply today. Even if you don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply - your passion and potential matter more than checking every box. Apply here: ----------

title: OPERATIONS MANAGER - Finance, Systems & Scale
description: OPERATIONS MANAGER The Nordstick (HepPros LLC) | Remote | Full-Time ABOUT THE NORDSTICK The Nordstick is a fast-growing DTC fitness equipment brand built around premium functional products like the NordBench Pro. We have grown 400%+ year over year and are scaling aggressively. Our operation runs on Shopify with a pre-sale model, a manufacturing partner in Hong Kong, and a 3PL network across multiple U.S. warehouse locations. Operations at The Nordstick is not admin work. It is cash flow management, inventory intelligence, execution speed, and margin protection. We are looking for an elite Operations Manager who can think like a CFO, execute like an operator, and build systems that scale. WHAT THIS ROLE IS (AND IS NOT) This role is not: --> Updating spreadsheets without context --> Reacting to problems after they happen --> Overbuying inventory "just in case" --> Managing ops without understanding cash flow This role is: --> Owning the 13-week cash flow forecast --> Making inventory decisions tied to demand and capital --> Using Shopify, data, and AI to stay ahead of issues --> Coordinating across multiple 3PLs for speed and margin --> Turning CX signals into product and process improvements --> Being the connective tissue between our manufacturer in Hong Kong, our 3PL partners, our CS team, and leadership WHO YOU ARE You are not just operationally great. You understand money. You know what cash on hand means, why contribution margin matters, and how inventory decisions ripple into the P&L. You have built financial models before, not just maintained them, and you can walk a founder through a cash flow forecast without needing a finance team behind you. You think in systems. You do not chase fires. You build the infrastructure that prevents them. When something breaks, you fix the root cause, not the symptom. You are comfortable with AI tools, not just as a user but as a builder. You have used Claude Code, Cursor, or similar tools to ship actual working systems, and you can maintain and improve what already exists. CORE RESPONSIBILITIES CASH FLOW AND FINANCIAL PLANNING --> Build and own a rolling 13-week cash flow model, updated weekly, covering in-stock and pre-sale scenarios --> Forecast inventory buys, marketing spend impact, loan repayments, and shipping and fulfillment costs --> Model best-, base-, and worst-case scenarios --> Model inventory financing decisions: Shopify Capital, working capital loans, supplier payment terms, and loan vs. payback rate tradeoffs --> Know cash on hand, weekly burn, weekly contribution margin, and profitability to one decimal at all times --> Ensure The Nordstick stays in stock without overbuying or locking up cash INVENTORY AND DEMAND FORECASTING --> Forecast demand using Shopify sales data, growth rates, seasonality, and marketing plans --> D ---------- when and how much to reorder to prevent stockouts that kill ---------- ntum and overstock that traps capital --> Manage POs from factory confirmation through container receipt, including ETD/ETA tracking and customs clearance via our freight forwarder --> Track batch-level inventory counts and maintain the allocation sheet as the source of truth for CS order messaging --> Monitor warehouse storage costs and manage dead inventory decisions in coordination with leadership WORKING CAPITAL AND GROWTH FINANCING --> Leverage Shopify Capital, working capital loans, and supplier terms strategically --> Provide units-on-hand and container count data for leadership's negotiations with the manufacturing partner --> Participate in tariff strategy decisions with the customs broker, including PSC filings and Section 232 duty refund coordination --> Balance growth speed with financial safety; capital is used strategically, not emotionally SHOPIFY AND SYSTEMS OWNERSHIP --> Be deeply fluent in Shopify Admin: order-level actions, SKU management, fulfillment status, and operational data --> Own operational data: orders, refunds, shipping costs, and inventory --> Build and maintain dashboards, Google Sheets models, and custom reports --> Bonus: ability to build custom dashboards or internal tools using Python, SQL, JavaScript, or Google Apps Script 3PL AND SHIPPING OPTIMIZATION --> Manage our 3PL relationships across multiple U.S. warehouse locations using ShipHero and ShipStation --> Maintain FIFO allocation rules across warehouses, manage priority-adjusted orders, and approve or deny partial shipments based on fulfillment logic --> Manage the warehouse-level approval process for inbound POs, including specifying which SKUs go to which warehouse location based on velocity and buffer strategy --> Track average shipping cost per unit weekly, by zone, and blended; reduce average shipping zones over time --> Evaluate per-unit carrier cost tradeoffs for bulk freight and individual shipments --> Maintain and update landed cost per unit as COGS, freight, and tariff conditions change --> Escalate and track fulfillment errors through to resolution CX TO OPS TO PRODUCT FEEDBACK LOOP --> Work closely with Customer Support to identify repeat product issues, confusion points, and return drivers --> Maintain the product issue and parts request tracker, categorized by defect type: product defect, instruction failure, info/expectation failure, and missing parts --> Track issue counts weekly and trend over time to surface whether product changes are reducing complaints --> Fix problems at the source by recommending improvements to instructional videos, setup guides, and product design --> Serve as the primary source of truth for CS on shipping timelines by product and order date range AI AND EFFICIENCY LEVERAGE --> Work hands-on with agentic AI tools, specifically Claude Code, to build, maintain, and improve internal operational systems --> Build and maintain existing dashboards and reporting tools; this is not a "use AI to summarize" role, it requires actual implementation work --> Automate reporting, flag anomalies, and reduce manual work across the ops function --> Identify new automation opportunities and scope them into working tools, not just proposals --> Follow the principle: AI handles repetition, humans make decisions WEEKLY REPORTING --> Produce a Weekly Ops State of the Union for the CEO covering: North Star KPI movement, inventory health, fulfillment dates, shipping zone breakdown, product issue counts, and 13-week cash runway --> Coordinate with marketing on customer lists tied to batch ship dates for email sends --> Work with finance on PO creation, payment coordination, and Shopify/ShipHero cleanup ahead of incoming shipments TOOLS YOU WILL USE DAILY --> Shopify Admin: order-level actions, SKU management, and fulfillment status --> ShipHero: warehouse inventory management, FIFO allocation, PO tracking, and partial shipment logic --> ShipStation: individual order shipment management --> Google Sheets: 13-week cash flow model, ops dashboard, allocation sheet, reshipment tracker, and shipment timeline tracker --> Slack: cross-functional coordination with CS, marketing, finance, and leadership --> Asana: task tracking and project management --> Richpanel: visibility into CS ticket data related to ops issues --> Freight forwarder portal: freight tracking and customs documentation --> Triple Whale: awareness of how ops data (COGS, shipping cost) affects profit reporting NORTH STAR KPIs You will be evaluated monthly on three metrics: --> Average Shipping Cost per Unit: direction: down month over month --> Average Time to Ship to Customer: direction: down month over month --> Product Reliability Index (product-related issues per 100 orders): direction: down month over month If two or more are improving, Ops is winning. If one or fewer are improving, we are not. No debate. No overrides. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Must-Haves: --> Proven experience in DTC or e-commerce operations, ideally with pre-sale or made-to-order inventory models --> Strong financial literacy: cash flow forecasting, margin analysis, working capital management --> Advanced Google Sheets skills; ability to build and maintain financial models with real data --> Shopify fluency: operations, not just navigation --> Experience managing inventory and fulfillment across multiple 3PLs --> Hands-on experience with agentic AI tools, specifically Claude Code; you must be able to build with it, not just prompt it --> Ability to build and maintain internal dashboards and operational reporting tools --> Systems thinker: you prevent problems, not chase them --> Strong communicator who proactively loops in CS, marketing, and leadership without being asked Strong Bonus Points: --> Built cash flow dashboards and models before; must be able to show samples --> Experience scaling fast-growing DTC brands --> AI-assisted coding experience (Python, SQL, JavaScript, or Google Apps Script using tools like Claude Code or Cursor) --> Experience working with freight forwarders and customs brokers --> Familiarity with ShipHero or a comparable WMS HOW WE MEASURE SUCCESS --> In-stock rate without cash strain --> Clean, accurate cash flow visibility at all times --> Lower shipping cost per order month over month --> Fewer CX issues caused by ops failures --> Faster decisions with less chaos HOW TO APPLY Send the following to ---------- --> Your resume --> An intro video, under 5 minutes, where you introduce yourself and answer why you believe you are a good fit for this role --> A link or sample of a cash flow model or financial dashboard you have built and maintained before --> A Loom or Zoom recording walking us through that sample work Applications without the sample work and video will not be reviewed.

title: Content Producer / Podcast Manager / Audio & Video Editor
job_title: Content Producer / Podcast Manager / Audio & Video Editor
description: ## About Boost Boost is building an ecosystem of tools and training for independent restaurants, coffee shops, and foodservice operators. Boost Back Office is already launched. It helps restaurant owners better understand and manage the operational numbers behind their business, including inventory, COGS, recipe costing, menu profitability, ordering, and related back-office workflows. Boost Academy is launching soon. It will provide practical, framework-based training for restaurant owners and operators, helping them understand their numbers, improve profitability, and run stronger businesses. Academy will also serve as the top of the funnel for Boost Back Office and, eventually, Boost Front Office. We are looking for a producer/editor/podcast manager who can help turn raw founder-led expertise into polished, useful, publishable content across Academy, social media, YouTube, podcast platforms, and other channels. ## Role Overview We are hiring a Content Producer / Podcast Manager / Audio & Video Editor  to edit and produce content for Boost Academy (course lessons), social media, YouTube, podcast-style content, interviews. The founder will provide the core expertise, frameworks, interviews, screen recordings, and raw audio/video. Your job is to turn that raw material into professional, clear, engaging content that can be published across multiple platforms. This role is part video editor, part content producer, part podcast manager, and part publishing operator. You do not need to own the whole growth strategy, but you do need to be organized, self-directed, detail-oriented, and able to move content from raw recording to finished asset without needing to be micromanaged. You will also help manage the podcast/interview workflow, including coordinating guests, preparing episodes for publishing, producing audio and video versions, and distributing public episodes to all relevant podcast and content platforms. ## What You’ll Own ### Video and Content Production * Editing founder-led videos * Editing interview-style content * Editing Boost Academy course lessons * Cutting long-form videos into short-form clips * Adding captions, titles, hooks, callouts, graphics, zooms, and light motion where useful * Cleaning up audio and improving pacing * Producing videos for YouTube, social media, ads, and course platforms * Formatting content for each platform * Publishing or scheduling content, depending on workflow * Managing content files, versions, exports, and asset organization * Creating reusable editing templates and production systems * Working with the Growth Lead to produce clips and assets based on current campaigns ### Podcast and Interview Management * Helping identify and organize potential podcast/interview guests * Managing guest outreach, scheduling, reminders, and follow-up * Coordinating recording logistics * Preparing guest information, episode notes, and production briefs * Producing full podcast/interview episodes from raw recordings * Creating audio-only podcast versions where appropriate * Creating video podcast versions for Academy, YouTube, and/or other platforms * Writing or preparing episode titles, descriptions, show notes, and timestamps * Creating short promotional clips from each episode * Preparing quote cards, episode graphics, or other promotional assets when needed * Publishing public episodes to all relevant podcast platforms and directories * Promoting episodes across YouTube, social channels, email , and other relevant channels * Maintaining a publishing calendar for podcast and interview content * Tracking episode status from idea to booked, recorded, edited, approved, published, and promoted ## Content Types You May Work On * Academy course lessons * Founder teaching videos * Restaurant profitability breakdowns * COGS/menu pricing videos * Screen recordings and software walkthroughs * Podcast-style interviews * Guest interviews with restaurant owners, operators, vendors, experts, and other relevant people * YouTube videos * Audio podcast episodes * Short-form social clips * Ad creative variations * Customer/community videos * Internal training or onboarding videos ## You Are a Good Fit If You * Can take raw footage and make it clear, polished, and engaging * Understand pacing, hooks, captions, and retention * Can edit educational content without making it feel boring * Can create short-form clips from longer recordings * Can work with screen recordings, talking-head videos, interviews, and course content * Understand basic podcast production workflows * Can manage guest scheduling and episode logistics without constant follow-up * Are organized with files, exports, naming conventions, publishing calendars, and deadlines * Can make judgment calls without needing every edit approved * Are comfortable working with a founder who provides rough material and expects you to help shape it * Can follow brand direction while also improving the output over time * Are reliable, communicative, and consistent ## What Success Looks Like Success in this role means Boost has a consistent content production machine. Key outcomes may include: * Course lessons edited and ready for Academy * Weekly long-form content published * Short-form clips produced from longer recordings * Podcast/interview episodes booked, produced, published, and promoted * Content delivered on schedule * Editing quality improves over time * Clear file organization and repeatable workflows * Founder time spent recording and creating, not editing, publishing, chasing guests, or managing production details * Growth Lead has enough creative assets to test ads and social angles ## Initial Priorities In the first 30 days, I would expect you to help with: * Creating a simple production workflow * Creating editing/export templates for recurring content types * Editing initial Academy lessons * Editing one long-form founder-led or interview-style video * Creating short-form clips from that content * Helping define file organization and handoff process * Setting up or improving the podcast/interview production workflow * Creating a system for guest outreach, booking, episode tracking, and publishing * Identifying any required tools, access, or missing assets ## Time and Work Expectations I care more about effective output than inflated hours. That said, any hours billed to Boost must be hours actively worked for Boost. I do not want overlapping billing, double-booked work, or a situation where someone says they are working eight hours for Boost while actually splitting that same block of time across multiple clients or jobs. I would rather pay more for fewer honest, focused hours than pay for a larger block of time that is not actually dedicated to this business. Please be clear about your real availability, preferred working arrangement, and how many focused hours per week you can reliably commit. ## To Apply Please do not send a generic cover letter. Instead, answer the questions below. 1. Describe your biggest win when it comes to producing, editing, repurposing, or managing content. Include what the raw material looked like, what you created from it, and the result. 2. Describe your biggest win when it comes to podcast, interview, YouTube, or long-form content production. Include your role in booking, producing, publishing, or promoting the content. 3. Explain what you would do in week one to get started quickly with Boost. Be specific. I am looking for how you organize, prioritize, and create ---------- ntum. 4. Explain what resources you would need to do this job that you do not have yet. This should not be a wish list. I only want the true requirements: access, tools, files, brand assets, software, information, or people you would need to perform well. 5. Share examples of long-form videos, short-form clips, course lessons, podcast/interview edits, ads, or social content you have produced. 6. Pick one example from your portfolio and explain your role in it. What did you receive, what did you change, and what decisions did you make? 7. If you have managed a podcast or interview show before, explain the workflow you used for guest booking, recording, editing, publishing, and promotion. 8. What does your ideal editing/production workflow look like from raw recording to final published asset? 9. How do you organize files, revisions, exports, episode assets, guest information, and content versions? 10. How would you promote a public podcast/interview episode after it is published? 11. How many focused hours per week can you realistically commit to Boost, and how do you handle time tracking or work logs? 12. Are you currently working with other clients or employers? If so, explain how you avoid overlapping work time and ensure billable hours are dedicated to the client being billed. 13. What kinds of content are you best at producing, and what kinds are outside your strengths? Applications that show strong examples, clear ownership, reliable production habits, and the ability to manage content from idea to publication will be prioritized.

title: Amazon PPC & Brand Manager
description: Amazon PPC & Brand Manager Remote | Full-time | Reporting directly to the CEO Read this first: If you're looking for a job where someone hands you a bid management spreadsheet and tells you which keywords to pause, keep scrolling. This isn't it. We're looking for someone who wants to **own the profitability of an entire Amazon business** (PPC, listings, launches, pricing, the whole thing) and who gets excited when they see a 14 day search term report with $400 of wasted spend, because they know exactly what to do with it. About us We're a profitable, growing consumer products brand on Amazon in the kitchen and family category. Our products are real tools, not toys or gimmicks, and they sit in tens of thousands of homes. We're a category leader in our niche. We're small, fast, and lean. No bloated agency layers. No politics. You'll talk to the CEO directly, every week. The role in one sentence: Every SKU in our catalog is as profitable as it can possibly be on Amazon, and that's on you. What you'll own: **PPC is the core of this role.** Sponsored Products, Brands, Display, Creator Connections. You pull the search term reports, you make the calls, you scale winners and cut losers. Every SKU has a target ACOS tied to its role in the business (evergreen, seasonal hero, year round with Q4 spike, liquidating) and you know the difference and you manage accordingly. **Listings and conversion.** CTR, conversion rate, keyword indexing, A+ content, main images. You flag what's underperforming, you brief the designer on exactly what you need, you split test monthly. **New product launches.** Listing, campaign, Vine, main image brief, all live at go live, nothing missing. You own the launch checklist and nothing slips. **Daily account health.** Suppressed listings, hijackers, prime badge, indexing, policy flags. You find it before we do. What success looks like in your first 90 days: - You've mapped every active SKU to a PPC objective and cleaned up the campaigns that don't match - Wasted spend is down, target ACOS is hit on 90%+ of SKUs, and you can tell us exactly why on the ones that aren't - Q4 listing plans are revamped with seasonal keywords, gifting angles, and holiday imagery, done before October - The CEO gets a daily pulse message she easily understands what is being done and why. - You've run at least two split tests and shared the results - Ran an deep analysis of the top 6 SKUs and identified and implemented growth levers (all assets and ppc) Who you are: - **2 to 5+ years doing Amazon PPC on a real catalog** (not one product, not theoretically, not just "I took a course") - Fluent in Sellerboard, Helium 10, or similar. Can pull a search term report and tell a story with it - You think in ACOS, TACOS, CVR, CTR, and BSR, and you know when each one matters and when it doesn't - You've optimized listings end to end: titles, bullets, backend, A+, indexing - You write in clear, professional English and communicate proactively (non negotiable: daily pulse, weekly snapshots) - You have opinions and you defend them with data - You work independently. Nobody will be checking on you. If that terrifies you, this isn't your role. If it excites you, keep reading. Bonus points: - Experience with Q4 heavy seasonal brands - Sponsored Brands video and Brand Store optimization - Experience with Creator Connections campaigns - You've launched new ASINs from zero to ranking What we offer: - Direct line to the CEO. No middle management, no bureaucracy - Full autonomy on PPC decisions within the strategy we set together - A profitable, growing brand with strong margins and room to scale - Long term role. We're building a team, not hiring and churning - Competitive compensation based on experience How to apply: Please submit an application through our official link here: ---------- Looking forward to learning more about you! We read every application that follows the instructions. We don't read the ones that don't.

Key metrics may include: * Cost per lead * Cost per Academy customer * Academy landing page conversion rate * Academy revenue from paid and organic channels * Email opt-in rate * Academy customer quality * Academy-to-Back-Office conversion rate * Back Office demos/trials generated from Academy * Winning ad angles identified * Winning content topics identified * Growth experiments completed per month ## Initial Priorities In the first 30 days, I would expect you to help with: * Auditing the current Boost positioning, offers, funnel, and content opportunities * Recommending the first flagship Academy offer to advertise * Defining the first 3–5 growth experiments * Creating the first paid social testing plan * Creating a simple weekly growth scorecard * Creating briefs for the producer/editor * Helping turn founder-led content into ads, social clips, email s, and funnel assets * Identifying what resources are required before we scale spend ## Time and Work Expectations I care more about effective output than hours. title: Supply & Inventory Managment
description: Supply & Inventory Management Manager Overview We are looking for an experienced Supply & Inventory Management Manager to take ownership of stock across a group of companies operating from multiple locations. This is a central, cross-functional role responsible for ensuring the right products are in the right place at the right time, across both physical warehouses and online marketplaces. You will sit at the heart of our operations, working across several ERP systems and sales channels to forecast demand, manage replenishment, control stock levels, and keep data accurate and reconciled across the group. Your decisions will directly drive availability, cash flow, and profitability, while reducing overstock, stockouts, and tied-up capital. This role suits someone who is highly numerate, systems-literate, and comfortable holding the bigger picture across multiple entities while also getting into the detail of individual SKUs, lead times, and supplier performance. Key Responsibilities Group-Wide Inventory Oversight Take overall responsibility for inventory across multiple companies, brands, and physical locations within the group. Maintain a single, reliable view of stock across all entities, reconciling discrepancies between systems, warehouses, and sales channels. Set and maintain minimum and maximum stock levels, safety stock, and reorder points for each location and channel. Implement consistent stock control processes, cycle counts, and stock takes across all sites. Demand Forecasting & Planning Forecast demand at SKU, channel, and location level using historical sales data, seasonality, promotions, and market trends. Factor in product lead times, supplier reliability, and manufacturing or shipping windows when planning purchasing and replenishment. Balance availability against working capital, avoiding both stockouts and excess holding. Plan ahead for peak periods, new product launches, and promotional activity across the group. ERP Systems & Data Management Manage and coordinate inventory data across multiple ERP systems used by different companies in the group. Ensure stock, purchasing, and sales data is accurate, consistent, and synchronised between systems and channels. Identify opportunities to standardise, integrate, or improve ERP and inventory workflows across the group. Act as a key point of contact for system data integrity, troubleshooting mismatches and driving process improvement. Marketplace & Online Channel Coordination Oversee inventory allocation and synchronisation across online marketplaces such as Amazon, Shopify, and TikTok Shop. Ensure stock is correctly distributed and listed across channels to maximise availability and sales without overselling. Coordinate with fulfilment and channel teams to align listings, stock feeds, and replenishment with demand. Monitor channel performance and adjust allocation strategies to protect margins and service levels. Replenishment & Lead Time Management Own the end-to-end replenishment process, raising and managing purchase orders in line with demand and lead times. Track inbound stock, follow up on overdue deliveries, and manage exceptions such as delays, shortages, or damaged goods. Continuously review supplier lead times and reliability, feeding this into planning and reorder logic. Supplier, 3PL & Warehouse Coordination Act as the main point of contact between suppliers, prep centres, and 3PL/warehouse partners across locations. Coordinate shipment schedules, inbound bookings, and stock transfers between sites and entities. Manage returns, damaged or missing goods, and associated supplier claims or refunds. Build strong working relationships with suppliers to improve terms, reliability, and responsiveness. Reporting & Analysis Develop and maintain key reporting on stock levels, stock value, turnover, ageing, availability, and forecast accuracy. Provide clear, regular reporting to leadership on inventory health and risks across the group. Use data to identify slow-moving and dead stock, recommend actions, and continuously improve inventory efficiency. Track and report on key metrics such as stock turn, sell-through, fill rate, and days of cover. Required Skills & Qualifications Minimum 2-3 years of hands-on experience in inventory, supply chain, or stock management, ideally across multiple locations or entities. Proven experience working with ERP and inventory management systems, including reconciling data across more than one platform. Strong demand forecasting and planning skills, with a solid grasp of lead times, reorder logic, and safety stock. Highly numerate and analytical, comfortable working with large datasets and turning them into clear decisions. Advanced spreadsheet skills (Excel/Sheets) and confidence with reporting and data tools. Experience managing inventory across online marketplaces such as Amazon, Shopify, or TikTok Shop. Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities across companies and locations. Strong communication and coordination skills, comfortable liaising with suppliers, 3PLs, and internal teams. Desirable Skills Experience working across a group structure with several companies, brands, or trading entities. Familiarity with multiple ERP systems and an understanding of how to integrate or standardise them. Knowledge of 3PL and prep centre operations. Experience with multichannel inventory or listing tools that sync stock across marketplaces. Understanding of cash flow and working capital implications of inventory decisions. A continuous-improvement mindset, with the ability to streamline processes and systems. Benefits Central, high-impact role with visibility across the whole group. Opportunity to shape inventory and supply processes across multiple companies and channels. Fast-paced, growing business with real ownership and autonomy. Ongoing professional development and growth opportunities. This position is ideal for someone who is organised, data-driven, and confident managing complexity across multiple companies, systems, and sales channels. If you enjoy bringing order to moving parts and using data to keep a growing operation stocked, efficient, and profitable, this role offers a challenging and rewarding opportunity.

description: ADVICE ASSOCIATE - FINANCIAL ADVICE INDUSTRY Location: Remote Type: Full-time Salary: $10-$15ph ABOUT LIFE UNSHACKLED LifeUnshackled is a platform built to help people reclaim the life they once dreamed of, clients and team alike. We exist because “retire comfortably” is not the goal, freedom is. We bring bold financial strategy and strong follow-through so clients can build real wealth and live life on their terms. You will be joining a growth-minded team that cares about ambition, high standards, and doing work that genuinely helps people unshackle their lives. ABOUT THE ROLE The Associate is the operational and relational lead for their assigned clients, acting as the Chief Operating Officer of each client relationship. This role combines precision in data and document management, project management discipline, people and communication skills, hands-on platform execution, and a delegation mindset. Each Associate is responsible for ensuring timely, compliant, and high-quality delivery of financial advice implementation and client outcomes, in coordination with the broader LifeUnshackled team. FOUR KEY AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITIES 1. The Information Steward - Custodian of all essential client information and access rights. - Curate and maintain a “Client Support Pack” with critical data and supporting documents for rapid use in preparing application forms. This includes identity documents (individuals and entities), FATCA, ABNs, ACNs, TFNs, ESAs, bank accounts, wholesale certificates, etc. - Collect and store tax-related and performance-related documentation (e.g. holding, distribution, loan, rental, annual, market value, tax statements). - Maintain and enforce the standard client folder structure, file naming conventions, and financial year categorisation so that files are audit-ready at all times. - Own the client Fact Find end-to-end — keeping it current after every meeting, statement, or client communication, and ensuring it underpins all advice documents as an auditable chain of evidence. - Monitor and update the real-time client balance sheet, sourcing data from various platforms and reconciling across systems quarterly. - Ensure adviser access and login credentials are in place and securely managed across all relevant platforms. - Collaborate with the PSM to standardise and streamline information management. - Mindset: “Would I be confident this is clean and client-ready at any time?” 2. The Delivery Project Manager - Leader of accurate client service implementation and delivery timelines. - Ensure investment transactions are implemented same-day and insurance applications are begun within 48 hours of approval. - Turn meeting actions and strategic goals into clearly written, trackable tasks — nothing falls through the cracks. - Own timelines and deadlines — chasing overdue tasks, flagging bottlenecks, and ensuring every task reaches a clear resolution. - Delegate technical or administrative tasks appropriately while owning the outcome. - Coordinate closely with paraplanners, the Practice Support Manager, the Principal Adviser, and external professionals. - Ensure documents and forms are completed correctly, on time, and sent to the right parties. - Mindset: “What’s needed to move this forward without needing Principal involvement?” 3. The Relationship Anchor - Point of continuity, context, and connection for each client. - Understand the needs and preferences of your clients and orchestrate effective service delivery accordingly. - Be the primary internal advocate and coordinator for your clients. - Track developments in the client’s personal and financial life. - Stay across all meeting notes and ensure task systems reflect meetings. - Notice changes in goals, mindset, or relationships and raise them with the Principal. - Support the Principal by ensuring they are well-informed before every meeting. - Ensure the client never has to repeat themselves or chase us for updates. - Mindset: “What’s shifted for the client that we haven’t yet actioned?” 4. The Compliant Storyteller - Ensuring each client file tells a compelling and compliant story. - Keep client files audit-ready with consistent, clear, and updated notes. - Manage the full post-meeting workflow: consent and transcription, file note generation and review, follow-up email s, and updating the Fact Find with any new information. - Ensure fact finds, SOAs, ROAs, and client communications are accurate and well-organised. - Maintain clarity in the chronology and context of advice decisions. - Highlight progress and transformation in the client’s journey, tying actions back to their goals. - Ensure documentation not only meets compliance and privacy standards but tells the narrative of value delivered. - Mindset: “Would this file make sense to an outsider, showing a clear and compliant story of impact?” PRIORITISATION ORDER - From a business perspective, your tasks should be prioritised in the following order: - Cash / investment transacting, including opening of associated accounts and completion of any KYC / onboarding requirements with third parties where this would delay a cash / investment transaction. - Insurance applications and getting policies into force. - Preparing meeting summaries and post-meeting email s for your clients, and any sub-10-minute tasks that are directly requested of you by the Principal Adviser. - Responding to requests made of us by other professionals (we expect fast responses from them and should return the favour). - Other work pertaining to clients who are in their first 6 weeks with us (including onboarding). - Other work pertaining to your broader client list, prioritised by the annual fee that they are paying us and any relationship considerations (including preparing their reports / maintaining their client file with current information / supporting loan applications / etc). - Balance this priority list with approaching deadlines — as deadlines near, the work becomes a higher priority. - Anything you can’t get to in a reasonable time, just flag it, and we can try to delegate to others or make a business decision to defer that task. REPORTING & COLLABORATION Reports to: Practice Support Manager (PSM) for delivery oversight; Principal Adviser for client outcomes. Collaborates with: PSM, Paraplanner, Admin Assistant, Principal Adviser. Indicators of Success - 100% of clients have complete, current documentation and adviser access. - Tasks are delivered on time with minimal Principal intervention. - High service ratings and positive feedback from assigned clients. - Accurate and timely handoff of technical and administrative work. - Adviser’s administrative workload is reduced for each client in your portfolio. - Investment transactions executed same-day; insurance applications commenced within 48 hours. - Demonstrated proficiency across all required platforms. Expected Behaviour - Proactive, reliable, and accountable. - Thoughtful and detail-oriented. - Able to prioritise and escalate as needed. - Collaborative, not siloed. - Focused on both client satisfaction and internal efficiency. APPLICATION PROCESS To apply, please submit the following: • A 2–5 minute video introducing yourself and explaining why you are the best fit for this role • Your updated CV and LinkedIn profile link • Names and contact details of three references (2 professional + 1 personal) Please apply and email all details to: ---------- ONLY those who follow the instructions in how to apply will be accommodated.

title: Finance Operations Assistant for UK Shopify Ecommerce — Xero / Long-Term Growth Role
job_title: Finance Operations Assistant for UK Shopify Ecommerce — Xero / Long-Term Growth Role
description: We're Kiln Crafts ( ---------- ), a UK-based ecommerce business selling pottery and ceramics supplies. We trade through Shopify, turn over more than £1m a year, and we're growing fast — which means the finance side of the business needs to grow with us. Our books sit in Xero. We use Dext (Hubdoc) for supplier invoices and A2X for Shopify reconciliation. We work with a UK accountant who handles VAT submission, payroll, and year-end. Your job is to own everything that sits between the day-to-day money movement and what the accountant needs. We are a small, friendly team and we believe in paying fair, treating people well, and growing roles long-term. This is not a short-term gig — we are looking for someone who wants to build a career with us as we scale. The Role — Now and Where It Grows This role starts at 40 hours per month (~10 hours per week) focused on core bookkeeping. As you prove yourself and the business grows, the role grows with you — both in scope and in hours. Stage 1 — Months 1 to 3 (your current scope): Weekly bank reconciliation across multiple accounts (business current, PayPal, Shopify Payments, Stripe) Process supplier invoices via Dext and code them correctly in Xero Reconcile Shopify sales and payouts via A2X Categorise expenses against our chart of accounts Prepare quarterly VAT data ready for our UK accountant to review and submit Maintain inventory journals and basic cost of goods entries Flag anything unusual the ---------- nt you spot it Stage 2 — Months 3 to 6 (the role expands): Supplier management — chasing invoices, tracking due dates, payment scheduling Customer payment chasing on B2B / trade accounts Quarterly subscription and software audit (we leak money on unused tools — your job to find it) Weekly management report on sales, margin, cash, and debtors Stage 3 — Months 6 to 12 (full finance operations): Refund and returns reconciliation (Shopify refunds to inventory) Shipping cost reconciliation (quoted vs actual carrier costs) Payroll prep for our UK accountant COGS hygiene as supplier prices change Petty cash and company card reconciliation Year 2 and beyond: This role can grow into a full-time Finance Operations role of 20–40 hours per week, with pay rising in line with hours and responsibility. We will commit to that path with the right person. Must Have 3+ years bookkeeping experience using Xero (certification strongly preferred) Proven experience with international ecommerce clients (Shopify, Amazon, Etsy) Working knowledge of A2X or similar (Link My Books, Synder) Comfortable with Dext / Hubdoc / Receipt Bank Strong written English — you will email suppliers, our accountant, and our team directly Reliable internet and a quiet place to work Self-managing — you run your patch, we don't micromanage Nice to Have UK VAT knowledge (you won't submit but you'll prep) Experience with inventory-heavy ecommerce businesses Familiarity with PayPal Business and Shopify Capital reconciliation Curiosity for spotting margin leaks, not just recording transactions Hours and Pay Starting hours: 40 hours per month (~10 hours per week) Starting pay: £250 / $315 USD per month Schedule: Flexible, but you must overlap at least 2 hours per day with UK business hours (4pm–6pm Manila time minimum) Payment: Bi-Weekly via Wise or Payoneer 13th-month pay and paid time off after a 3-month probation period Reviews every 6 months with structured pay rises as hours and responsibility grow We are very serious about this being a long-term, growing role. We'd rather pay one excellent person well and grow them than churn through cheap hires. How To Apply To show me you've read this post properly, please do all five of the following — applications that miss any of these will not be reviewed: Subject line: "Kiln Crafts Finance Ops Application — [Your Name]" In the first line of your message, tell me what A2X does in one sentence List the Xero ecommerce clients you've worked with (no names needed — just industry and rough turnover) State your Xero certification status and date achieved Share your CV and your weekly availability in UK time Looking forward to hearing from you.

description: We run a remote tech support service for seniors 65 and older in the U.S. We help older adults with their phones, computers, and tablets by phone. Our customers are loyal and relationships drive everything. We are hiring ONE person to own our sales pipeline. You will respond to leads fast, follow up until you get a yes or a no, handle objections, and ask for the sale every time. This is real sales. You will be measured on members closed. Pushy tactics do not work with seniors. Warm persistence does. YOU ARE THE RIGHT FIT IF YOU: Have a proven track record in sales with real numbers to share Confidently ask for the sale every time Handle objections through value, not pressure Follow up relentlessly and never let a lead go cold Are genuinely warm and patient with older adults (non-negotiable) Speak clear, easy-to-understand English over the phone Are self-managing and hit your numbers without being chased DO NOT APPLY IF YOU: Have never closed sales or have no numbers to show Need heavy supervision to stay on task Are not comfortable on the phone most of the day Have background noise or a poor audio setup WHAT YOU WILL DO EACH DAY: Respond to every new lead within 1 hour by phone and text Make outbound calls and follow up with past leads Run intro calls, handle objections, and close the sale Post in senior and caregiver Facebook groups to attract leads Log all activity in our CRM daily Send a short report each evening WHAT WE PROVIDE: Proven sales scripts and full training All tools paid for: CRM, texting platform, calling system Daily check-in with your manager TECH REQUIREMENTS (must have before day one): Windows 10 or newer, OR Mac macOS 11 or newer (no Chromebooks or tablets) Intel Core i5 or AMD Ryzen 5 minimum, 8GB RAM minimum Internet: 25 Mbps download and 10 Mbps upload minimum (run a speed test) USB or 3.5mm headset with microphone (no earbuds, no speakerphone) Quiet dedicated workspace for calls during U.S. business hours COMMISSION (paid monthly, one-time per new member): 1 to 10 members closed: $5 each 11 to 20 members closed: $8 each 21 or more members closed: $15 each Commission is a one-time payout only. It is not recurring. Free trials and guest signups do not count. A member must be active and paying for 30 days before commission is paid. HOW TO APPLY: Start your message with the word SUNRISE or you will not be reviewed Share your sales numbers: best month, close rate, and what you sold Tell us in 2 to 3 sentences about a time you turned a no into a yes List your available hours in U.S. time zones and your internet speed from a test taken today Background noise in your voice recording is an automatic disqualifier. WAGE: $720/month base ($4.50/hr, 40 hrs/week) plus commission HOURS: 40 hours per week, U.S. business hours

title: [CEBU BASED] Amazon Account Manager (Customer Service & Admin)
job_title: [CEBU BASED] Amazon Account Manager (Customer Service & Admin)
description: QUICK HIGHLIGHTS - Role: Join a profitable, fast-growing e-commerce brand as the detail-obsessed operator behind our customer service, admin, and Amazon operations. Our AI systems do the heavy lifting; you keep them honest and handle what they can't. - Stage: Profitable, 12-year-old e-commerce business selling across 4 Amazon marketplaces (US, UK, DE, IRL), with consistent 30% YoY growth. - Team: A lean team of A-Players in our Cebu office. Your work directly impacts company performance. - Location & Schedule: Full-time and 100% on-site at our Cebu office, 11:00am to 8:00pm, Monday to Friday. This is not a remote or hybrid role, and there are no exceptions. Please only apply if you're based in Cebu and happy working from an office every day. - Compensation: $800 to $1,120/month depending on experience, plus benefits (13 paid leave days, all PH holidays, HMO, performance-based 13th month, paid weekly). - Why now: We've automated a huge amount of our operations. What's left needs a sharp, reliable human: the judgment calls, the customer conversations, the daily checks that keep everything running clean. A QUICK NOTE ON THE TITLE We've called this an Amazon Account Manager role because that's the background we want you to have. In practice it's broader than a pure Amazon job. Day to day, this is a customer service and admin role first, with Amazon operations as a core part of it. We specifically want someone who has worked inside Amazon Seller Central, because that experience and instinct is genuinely valuable to us, even though you won't be living in Amazon all day. If you have that background and you also love clean admin and great customer service, this is for you. ABOUT THE ROLE The heart of this job is customer service and admin, done to a very high standard. You'll handle customer and partner conversations our automated systems can't (with good judgment and excellent written English), keep our inboxes and records clean, run daily checks on our automated systems and flag anything off, and support our Amazon operations: Seller Central housekeeping, case follow-through, account-health monitoring. You'll also be cross-trained to run customer service solo when our ops lead is on leave: real responsibility, real trust. This is a junior role with real room to grow into Amazon and e-commerce operations. What matters is not years of experience; it's accuracy, follow-through, and catching the thing nobody else noticed. YOU'D BE A FIT IF YOU... - Have 1+ year experience with Amazon Seller Central (VA, account admin, or CS role). You know your way around; you don't need to be a specialist. - Have real customer service experience: you write clear, warm, professional replies and know when a situation needs escalating. - Are detail obsessed: you catch errors before anyone else sees them. - Follow SOPs exactly, and notice when the SOP itself is broken. - Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) to work our systems. - Write excellent English. NOT A FIT IF... - You're looking for remote, hybrid, or work-from-home arrangements. This role is on-site in Cebu, every day, no exceptions. - You're primarily focused on PPC, creative, content, or brand strategy. - You want to build automations and AI systems (we have that covered; this role operates them). - You're looking for a senior catalog or account management position (this is a junior role). - You need constant supervision, or dislike process, repetition, and detailed data tasks. - You're agency-based or juggling multiple clients. RESPONSIBILITIES - Customer Service: handle the conversations our systems can't, in our brand voice, with judgment; cross-trained for solo CS cover when our ops lead is on leave. - Admin Excellence: inboxes, reports, dashboards, data hygiene the team can trust, zero unforced errors. - Systems Monitoring: daily checks on our automated systems; anything off gets flagged within one working day. - Amazon Support: Seller Central housekeeping, case resolution with persistence and follow-through, account-health monitoring. - Accurate time records and clean categorization, every day (we run on trust plus good data). Attention to detail is critical for this role. We're looking for someone who actually reads job descriptions carefully, so when the form asks what your favorite number is, the answer is 99. WHY JOIN US - Clarity, not guesswork: You'll always know what's expected and where you stand. Clear SOPs, clear targets, fast and direct feedback. - Your work gets seen: We measure work closely. If you take pride in accuracy and follow-through, good work gets noticed and rewarded, not lost. - Stability: A profitable, 12-year-old business that pays weekly, on time, every time. - Learning: Work directly with experienced e-commerce operators and modern AI tools every day. - Culture: Low-drama. High-clarity. Feedback-friendly. Do good work, get treated like an adult. HOW TO APPLY To apply, please complete this short application form: ---------- Apply through the form only. Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed. WHAT HAPPENS NEXT 1. We review your application form. 2. Initial conversation. 3. Deep dive into your Amazon and customer service experience. 4. Practical work-sample exercise (realistic scenarios from the actual role). 5. Final round interview on site in our Cebu office with leadership and culture fit.

title: Finance Director
description: This is a chance to do high-grade finance work for some of the most exciting growth companies in the CPG and DTC space. CFO Pod Support and Client Coverage •        Serve as the primary analytical partner to Client CFOs across multiple engagements. •        Prepare materials and analysis ahead of board meetings, investor calls, and strategic planning sessions. •        Support client meetings alongside the CFO, and over time step into functional conversations with heads of marketing, supply chain, and operations as trust is built. •        Provide guidance and decision support on commercial questions including pricing, channel mix, inventory planning, and vendor terms. 4. Capital Markets and Strategic Support •        Support fundraising and M&A processes by building investor materials, data rooms, credit packs, and diligence support. •        Assist with capital allocation scenarios, cash runway planning, and lender and investor reporting packages. What we're looking for: Candidates must be comfortable working directly with CFOs and supporting multiple client engagements •        6 to 8 years of progressive experience in FP&A, financial operations, or corporate finance, with a track record of owning planning cycles and recurring reporting end to end. •        Senior FP&A or controllership-trained background. You are as comfortable with the integrity of the underlying data as with the model built on top of it. •        Prior experience in a multi-client or portfolio support role (fractional, consulting, PE operating, or multi-entity environment) is strongly preferred. •        Deep understanding of consumer business models including DTC, retail, omnichannel, and wholesale. •        Advanced financial modeling skills, including multi-year three-statement models and scenario analysis. •        Strong working knowledge of accounting principles (accrual vs. cash, revenue recognition, COGS treatment, inventory accounting). •        Experience with accounting platforms (QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Xero) and BI or reporting tools. •        Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, executive-ready insights and communicate with confidence to senior stakeholders. •        Bonus: strong experience with LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT) and automation platforms. •        Thrives in a lean, high-performance, distributed team environment. title: SEO Content Operations Manager (QA and Editing)
job_title: SEO Content Operations Manager (QA and Editing)
description: Good work should win the work. Rootl helps trades and local service businesses get found, picked and booked online. We exist because good businesses lose to worse ones every day. Not because they're worse at the job, but because the worse ones got found first. It started with advice from an upstairs window to a window cleaner halfway up a ladder. By 2036 we want Rootl to be the UK's most trusted local search company for trades, with our first US hub open. We're building the team that gets us there. Want a seat on the bus? WHAT WE DO We help trades and local service businesses get found on Google, and inside the AI tools their next customer is already searching with: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini. That is the job. We work with plumbers, gas engineers, roofers, joiners, plasterers, drainage crews, window firms, waste and pest control, architects, developers and taxi firms. We run three services, Essentials, Growth and Accelerator, all pointed at one thing: putting our client in front of the customer who is already searching. THE ROLE, IN ONE LINE You own how we deliver. You run our content production from brief to published page across every client, keeping the quality high and the pipeline moving. READ THIS TWICE: THIS IS NOT A WRITING JOB Our AI tools do the heavy drafting. We are not looking for a writer with flair. We need someone who can take a draft and make it genuinely client-ready. That means catching errors, tightening the copy, fixing the SEO, and making sure nothing wrong or sloppy ever reaches a client. The detail is the deliverable. A STRAIGHT WORD ABOUT THIS ROLE This is a brand new seat, and we are building it as we go. The founder needs to step out of the day to day and focus on where Rootl is heading and how we get there. That leaves a real gap, and it is yours to fill. So be clear on what you are walking into. We are moving fast and we do not have every answer yet. Some weeks will feel like organised chaos. This role exists to bring order to it. If that excites you rather than worries you, and you are the sort who turns chaos into a clean, repeatable system, this is your seat. It is a rocket ship, and we want you on board. WHY YOU'D WANT THIS SEAT - A small, focused team built around getting one job done brilliantly. James runs sales and strategy. Our web developer builds the sites. You own the SEO content production system end to end. Three people, three clear lanes, no politics, no meetings about meetings. - Real responsibility from day one. This is not a six-month shadow-the-founder role. - The work is simple by design. It is a series of checklists. We want someone who finds that energising, not boring. - You will not be slotted into someone else's process. You will write the process, recorded with the founder and turned into the Blueprints and SOPs every future Rootl hire is trained on. - Real long-term upside for the person who stays the course. We will talk that through properly once you are established. - Local search is shifting under everyone's feet right now. We are moving fast on it, and you will be at the front. - We hire the right person, not the perfect person. Every candidate is DISC profiled, because the seat has to fit how we work. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Running our content agent and editing its output to a publish-ready standard - Quality checking every page before it goes ---------- facts, spelling, grammar, British English, tone, and on-page SEO - Working from SEO briefs and making sure each page does the job it is meant to do - Managing our web developer: answering their questions, handing over finished pages, keeping the build on track - Spotting local SEO improvements (Google Business Profile, on-page, internal links) and flagging them - Owning the schedule: what is due, for which client, by when, and hitting it - Running your part of our weekly tea ---------- eting - Taking our SOPs and making the process tighter over time WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR - You spot a wrong town or city name, a missing full stop, or a clumsy sentence from a mile off. Detail is your thing. - You would rather follow a proven checklist and run it well than reinvent the wheel each time. - You take pride in doing similar work to a high standard, week in, week out. - You check your own work before anyone else sees it. Things do not slip past you. - You can take an SOP and run with it without being chased. - You want a long-term home where you can own something, not a stepping stone. - Excellent written British English. We will test this. - Solid on-page SEO: titles, meta descriptions, headings, internal links, alt text, basic schema. - Comfortable editing AI-written content: cutting repetition, fixing flat phrasing, removing the AI tells, and fact-checking. Nice to have, not essential: - Local SEO or Google Business Profile experience - Experience optimising content to get picked up by AI answers (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) - WordPress TOOLS YOU WILL USE Our content agent, WordPress, Google Workspace, Local Dominator, BrightLocal, and AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. Training and SOPs provided. You do not need every tool on day one, but you do need to learn fast. HOURS, PAY AND HOW IT WORKS - Part-time to start, around 10 to 15 hours a week, paid at $8 USD an hour. - We start with a short unpaid test task so we can see how you work. If it goes well, you move onto a two-week paid trial, paid for the hours you actually work. - Once you pass the trial, we guarantee 40 hours a month as a floor, so there is always a baseline you can count on. In practice you will usually do more. Your hours and your rate both grow as you prove yourself and as we sign more clients, and the aim is to build this into a full-time seat for the right person. - If a client ever leaves and the work drops, we give you at least one week's written notice of any change to your hours. - Paid weekly for your first month, then monthly after that, by Wise. - You track your time in Toggl. Your tracked hours are what you invoice, so it stays clear and fair on both sides. - Every Monday, without fail, we run a 30 minute tea ---------- eting using the LIONS sheet. It is a simple one-page worksheet covering five things: Last week, Issues, Opportunities, the Next seven days, and Successes. You fill yours in and come ready to run your part. If you are ever away, you still send your completed sheet before the meeting. It keeps us aligned and the work on track. - We work UK hours, 9:00 to 4:30. At least half your hours each week need to fall inside that window so we can work together properly. For you in the Philippines that is roughly 4pm to 11:30pm, so an evening pattern fits well. - This is an independent contractor role on a proper written agreement covering confidentiality, client data, and how we pay you. You look after your own taxes in the Philippines, and you provide your own computer, reliable internet, and a quiet place to work. - Four weeks' notice on either side if it is ever not working out. HOW TO APPLY - Start your application with the phrase "I spotted it" so we know you have read this far. - Tell us, in a few lines, about a time you caught a mistake everyone else had missed. - Share any examples of editing, proofreading, or SEO content work you are proud of. - If you get through this first stage, we will send you a short test task: a real page with a few errors planted in it, for you to fix and explain. This first task is unpaid and the same for everyone. If it goes well, the paid trial follows. A LAST WORD We are not the biggest name out there, and we are not trying to be. We are here to show what local search looks like when it is done properly, and we want to be the best in the country at it. We are looking for the person who helps us get there. If you have read this far and something here lit you up, that is a good sign. We read every application that opens the right way. Show us why it should be you. Want a seat on the bus?

job_title: Remote Civil/Electrical Design Engineer — Site Civil, Stormwater & Mission-Critical Equipment Layout (U.S. Projects, U.S
description: Good addition — but one scope judgment first, because it changes who you’re actually hiring. Stormwater/site-civil and mission-critical power are two different disciplines. A civil engineer’s legitimate role with generators, MV/HV gear, and 480V is the site/civil side: equipment pads and foundations, fuel storage and secondary containment (SPCC), spill berms around transformers, equipment-yard grading and drainage, MV/HV duct bank and conduit routing layouts, NEC/NESC working-clearance and access geometry, and delivery/laydown access roads. That’s real and worth requiring. What this person should not own is the electrical design — generator paralleling, switchgear sizing, load flow, and the MV-vs-480V topology. That’s electrical-EOR work and belongs in your MEP RFP track. Note for consistency: at 10 MW/site your campus distribution is MV (12.47 kV); 480V is the utilization/generator-output level, not the distribution backbone — so the posting should say “understands” 480V and MV equipment, not “designs the 480V distribution system.” If you want one offshore hire wearing both hats, the practical version is a dual-discipline design engineer/drafter who does civil site work and electrical CAD (one-lines, equipment layouts, duct banks) under separate civil-PE and electrical-PE direction. Here’s that posting: Job Posting (revised — copy/paste) Title: Remote Civil/Electrical Design Engineer — Site Civil, Stormwater & Mission-Critical Equipment Layout (U.S. Projects, U.S. Hours) About the role: We develop distributed digital-infrastructure (data center) campuses across rural Missouri. We need an experienced design engineer to produce site-civil, stormwater, and mission-critical equipment-siting deliverables for multiple ~5–50 acre campuses, each carrying standby generators, medium-voltage transformers, switchgear, and battery energy storage. Long-term, full-time, remote, working U.S. Central Time hours (8:00 AM–5:00 PM CT), under the direction of U.S.-licensed civil and electrical PEs who review and seal all permit submittals. Responsibilities — Site Civil & Stormwater: • Grading, drainage, and site-development plans • Stormwater design: detention/retention basins, storm sewer, culverts, catch basins, hydraulic grade line checks • Pre/post-development runoff analysis (NRCS TR-55/TR-20, NOAA Atlas 14) • SWPPP and erosion/sediment control exhibits; earthwork and pipe sizing Responsibilities — Mission-Critical Equipment Siting (civil/layout scope): • Equipment pad and foundation layouts for standby generators, MV transformers, switchgear, and BESS units • Fuel storage siting and secondary/spill containment (SPCC) design • Equipment-yard grading, drainage, and oil-water separation around HV/transformer areas • MV/HV and 480V duct bank, conduit, and cable-trench routing layouts • NEC working clearances and NESC high-voltage clearance/access geometry; equipment delivery and laydown access roads • Production of equipment layout drawings and electrical one-line drafting under an electrical PE’s direction Nice to have: Data center / mission-critical / industrial site experience, Bluebeam Revu, GIS, U.S. county/state submittal sets, REVIT.

description: Good addition — but one scope judgment first, because it changes who you’re actually hiring. Stormwater/site-civil and mission-critical power are two different disciplines. A civil engineer’s legitimate role with generators, MV/HV gear, and 480V is the site/civil side: equipment pads and foundations, fuel storage and secondary containment (SPCC), spill berms around transformers, equipment-yard grading and drainage, MV/HV duct bank and conduit routing layouts, NEC/NESC working-clearance and access geometry, and delivery/laydown access roads. That’s real and worth requiring. What this person should not own is the electrical design — generator paralleling, switchgear sizing, load flow, and the MV-vs-480V topology. That’s electrical-EOR work and belongs in your MEP RFP track. Note for consistency: at 10 MW/site your campus distribution is MV (12.47 kV); 480V is the utilization/generator-output level, not the distribution backbone — so the posting should say “understands” 480V and MV equipment, not “designs the 480V distribution system.” If you want one offshore hire wearing both hats, the practical version is a dual-discipline design engineer/drafter who does civil site work and electrical CAD (one-lines, equipment layouts, duct banks) under separate civil-PE and electrical-PE direction. Here’s that posting: Job Posting (revised — copy/paste) Title: Remote Civil/Electrical Design Engineer — Site Civil, Stormwater & Mission-Critical Equipment Layout (U.S. Projects, U.S. Hours) About the role: We develop distributed digital-infrastructure (data center) campuses across rural Missouri. We need an experienced design engineer to produce site-civil, stormwater, and mission-critical equipment-siting deliverables for multiple ~5–50 acre campuses, each carrying standby generators, medium-voltage transformers, switchgear, and battery energy storage. Long-term, full-time, remote, working U.S. Central Time hours (8:00 AM–5:00 PM CT), under the direction of U.S.-licensed civil and electrical PEs who review and seal all permit submittals. Responsibilities — Site Civil & Stormwater: • Grading, drainage, and site-development plans • Stormwater design: detention/retention basins, storm sewer, culverts, catch basins, hydraulic grade line checks • Pre/post-development runoff analysis (NRCS TR-55/TR-20, NOAA Atlas 14) • SWPPP and erosion/sediment control exhibits; earthwork and pipe sizing Responsibilities — Mission-Critical Equipment Siting (civil/layout scope): • Equipment pad and foundation layouts for standby generators, MV transformers, switchgear, and BESS units • Fuel storage siting and secondary/spill containment (SPCC) design • Equipment-yard grading, drainage, and oil-water separation around HV/transformer areas • MV/HV and 480V duct bank, conduit, and cable-trench routing layouts • NEC working clearances and NESC high-voltage clearance/access geometry; equipment delivery and laydown access roads • Production of equipment layout drawings and electrical one-line drafting under an electrical PE’s direction Nice to have: Data center / mission-critical / industrial site experience, Bluebeam Revu, GIS, U.S. county/state submittal sets, REVIT.

title: Packaging & Box Designer - Remote Contractor
description: About Kadia Fulfillment Kadia Fulfillment is a fast-growing gifting studio and brand operations company based in Dallas, Texas. We design, assemble, and ship custom PR boxes, influencer gifting campaigns, and retail gift collections for beauty, lifestyle, and fashion brands across the United States. Our clients include brands distributed through Macy's, Bloomingdale's, and sold on Amazon and direct-to-consumer. We are expanding our creative team and are looking for a talented, detail-obsessed packaging and box designer to join us as a remote contractor. This role is critical — the design of our boxes is the first thing an influencer sees, and it determines whether they post or not. The Role We are hiring a Packaging & Box Designer on a project-by-project contract basis. You will be responsible for creating the visual design and structural layout (dieline) of custom gift boxes, mailer boxes, and inserts for our client campaigns. You will work closely with our studio director to bring each campaign's creative brief to life in a way that is beautiful, on-brand, and print-ready. This is a remote, part-time contractor position. You will be paid per project. As Kadia grows, high-performing designers will have the opportunity for more frequent and larger projects. What You'll Be Designing Custom gift boxes (rigid, collapsible, magnetic closure, sleeve boxes) Custom mailer boxes (corrugated, e-commerce style) Box inserts — tray liners, foam inserts, dividers, crinkle fill layouts Printed tissue paper with custom patterns or branding Branded cards, thank-you notes, product cards, and stickers Custom ribbon and label designs 3D mockup renderings for client approval before production Requirements — Must Have Adobe Illustrator — Expert level. All dielines and print files must be delivered in .AI or .PDF format. This is non-negotiable. Adobe Photoshop — Proficient. Used for 3D box mockup creation and visual presentations for client approval. Dieline Knowledge — Must understand box construction and how a flat dieline becomes a 3D box. Experience with structural packaging design required. Print Specifications — Must know CMYK color mode, bleed (3mm minimum), safe zone, resolution (300 DPI minimum), and print-ready file setup. Portfolio — Must include at least 3 examples of packaging or box design work. Rigid boxes, gift boxes, or mailer boxes preferred. English Communication — Must be able to read and understand creative briefs written in English and communicate clearly via email or Slack. Turnaround Time — Must be able to deliver first drafts within 3–5 business days of receiving the brief. Rush turnaround of 48 hours required occasionally. Nice to Have (Bonus Skills) Experience with packaging for beauty, cosmetics, or skincare brands Canva Pro proficiency for client-facing mockup presentations Experience with printing supplier portals — Lumi, Packlane, PakFactory 3D rendering skills — Cinema 4D, Blender, or Keyshot — for photorealistic mockups Structural engineering knowledge for complex box constructions Experience designing for both US and overseas manufacturers How Projects Work Step 1 — Brief Sent: Kadia sends you a written creative brief including brand colors, campaign theme, box size, number of pieces, materials, and reference images. Step 2 — First Draft: You deliver 1–2 design concepts in 3–5 business days. Deliverables are a flat design on dieline (.AI file) and a 3D mockup image (.JPG or .PNG). Step 3 — Revisions: Up to 2 rounds of revisions are included. Additional revisions are billed at an agreed hourly rate. Step 4 — Print-Ready File: Final approved design delivered as a print-ready PDF (CMYK, 300 DPI, with bleed and crop marks) AND an editable .AI source file. Step 5 — Payment: Payment sent via PayPal or Wise within 3 business days of final file delivery and approval. Compensation Simple mailer box design (1 piece) — $80 to $150. One dieline and 3D mockup. Straightforward brand application. Gift box with insert design (2–3 pieces) — $150 to $300. Box, tray liner, and insert card. Most common project type. Full campaign kit (5+ pieces) — $300 to $600. Box, tissue, card, sticker, ribbon, and outer wrap. Full gifting studio package. Rush delivery (48 hours) — add 25% on top of the base rate. Must confirm availability first. Top performers who deliver consistently and build trust with our team will receive first priority on all new projects and may be offered a monthly minimum guarantee as volume grows. How to Apply Please submit your application with the following: Portfolio link or PDF At least 3 specific examples of box or packaging work Your rates per project type Your average turnaround time
